source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which photoreceptors in the retina are responsible for night and peripheral vision?
questions.rationale: Rods handle peripheral, dark and night vision; cones handle central, day and color vision.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Eye anatomy (PDF p. 428)
questions.quote: rods (peripheral vision, dark and night vision) and cones (central vision, day and colored vision).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client's Snellen result is 20/200 in the better eye even with glasses. This means:
questions.rationale: He reads at 20 feet what a normal eye reads at 200 feet; 20/200 is legal blindness and disqualifies driving.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Snellen test (PDF p. 429)
questions.quote: Result of 20/200 indicates legal blindness. This disqualifies the client from driving.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which test screens for red-green color blindness?
questions.rationale: Ishihara plates show numbers made of colored dots that a color-blind person cannot read.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ishihara plate (PDF p. 429)
questions.quote: It can assess red and green color blindness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Tonometry is done to measure:
questions.rationale: Tonometry indirectly measures IOP (normal about 11–21 mmHg); raised values suggest glaucoma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Tonometry (PDF p. 429)
questions.quote: Indirect measure of intraocular pressure (IOP). Normal is 11-21 mmHg.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During ophthalmoscopy, the red reflex is absent in one eye. This suggests:
questions.rationale: An absent red reflex suggests opacity of the lens, as in cataract (or retinoblastoma in children).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ophthalmoscopy (PDF p. 430)
questions.quote: Absence of red reflex may indicate opacity of the lens.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A painful, red swelling on the eyelid margin is most likely a:
questions.rationale: A hordeolum is a staphylococcal infection of a lash follicle and is painful; a chalazion is a painless hard lump.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Eye disorders (PDF p. 430)
questions.quote: It is characterized by painful, red swelling on the eyelid margin.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A 70-year-old has gradual, painless blurring of vision, like looking through frosted glass. The likely cause is:
questions.rationale: Cataract is lens opacity causing gradual blurring; surgery (phacoemulsification with lens implant) is the treatment.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Cataract (PDF p. 430)
questions.quote: It causes blurring of vision which may progress to blindness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After cataract surgery, which activity should the client avoid?
questions.rationale: Bending, stooping, heavy lifting, straining and rubbing the eye raise intraocular pressure.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Postoperative eye care (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: Bending, stooping.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After cataract surgery, the client is best positioned:
questions.rationale: Avoid pressure on the operated eye and contamination of the dressing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Postoperative eye care (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: Position the client supine or turned to the unaffected side.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Hours after eye surgery, the client reports sharp eye pain and a feeling of pressure. The nurse should:
options: Report it to the surgeon at once
Reassure him it is the anesthetic
questions.rationale: Sharp pain with pressure suggests bleeding into the eye and must be reported immediately.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Postoperative eye care (PDF p. 432)
questions.quote: Sensation of pressure within the eye and sharp pain in the eye indicate bleeding.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client sees floaters and flashes of light, then a curtain over part of his vision. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Floaters, flashes and a curtain-like shadow are classic for retinal detachment; urgent surgery is needed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Retinal detachment (PDF p. 432)
questions.quote: There is sensation that a curtain has been drawn before the eyes

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: The early visual loss in open-angle glaucoma is:
questions.rationale: Glaucoma first causes loss of peripheral vision; blindness is irreversible due to optic nerve damage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Glaucoma (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: Loss of peripheral vision initially (tunnel vision), then blindness occurs.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has sudden severe eye pain, halos around lights, nausea and a fixed, mid-dilated pupil. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Acute closed-angle glaucoma is an emergency: sudden pain, halos, nausea and a fixed dilated pupil.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Glaucoma (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: Fixed, dilated pupil in acute glaucoma.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How does pilocarpine treat glaucoma?
questions.rationale: Miotics pull the iris away from the angle so aqueous humor can drain; acetazolamide and timolol reduce production.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Glaucoma management (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: To constrict the pupils, draw the iris away from the canal of Schlemm. This permits drainage of aqueous humor.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug should the nurse question for a client with glaucoma?
questions.rationale: Atropine, diphenhydramine and benztropine dilate the pupil and block aqueous outflow ("avoid ABC").
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Glaucoma (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: In glaucoma, avoid ABC: A- tropine B- enadryl C- ogentin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older adult says straight lines look wavy and the center of his vision is blurred. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Macular degeneration causes loss of central vision; glaucoma affects peripheral vision first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Macular degeneration (PDF p. 433)
questions.quote: Is manifested by loss of central vision.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A 48-year-old now holds the newspaper at arm's length to read. This is due to:
questions.rationale: Presbyopia is loss of accommodation from a hardening lens with age; convex reading glasses correct it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Refraction errors (PDF p. 434)
questions.quote: Presbyopia is loss of accommodation due to hardening of the lens.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lens corrects myopia (nearsightedness)?
questions.rationale: In myopia light focuses in front of the retina; a concave lens corrects it. Hyperopia needs a convex lens.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Refraction errors (PDF p. 434)
questions.quote: It requires concave lens.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Muriatic acid splashed into a worker's eye. The first action is to:
questions.rationale: Immediate, copious irrigation with water removes the chemical and limits damage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Eye trauma (PDF p. 434)
questions.quote: Immediate copious flushing of the eye with water if acid, alkali or other irritating substances had been introduced into the eyes.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A glass splinter is stuck in a client's cornea. The nurse should:
options: Cover the eyes loosely; refer at once
Press a tight patch on it
questions.rationale: Do not remove an embedded object; cover the eyes loosely to limit movement and get immediate medical care.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Eye trauma (PDF p. 434)
questions.quote: If foreign body is lodged into the cornea, do not attempt to remove it (e.g. glass splinters).

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When guiding a blind client to walk, the nurse should:
options: Lead a step ahead, arm offered
questions.rationale: The nurse walks a step ahead while the client holds her arm, giving safety and a sense of direction. Speak before touching.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Care of the blind (PDF p. 435)
questions.quote: When assisting the client in ambulation, the nurse should be a step ahead of the client.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: On Rinne's test, the client hears the tuning fork longer on the mastoid bone than near the ear canal. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Normally air conduction is better than bone; bone better than air suggests conductive loss (e.g., otosclerosis).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Rinne's test (PDF p. 435)
questions.quote: Conductive hearing loss: bone conduction is better than air conduction

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: In Weber's test, sound lateralizes to the left ear, which has poor hearing. This suggests:
options: Conductive loss in the left ear
Sensorineural loss in the left ear
questions.rationale: In conductive loss the tone is heard better in the poorer ear; in sensorineural loss, in the better ear.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Weber's test (PDF p. 436)
questions.quote: Conductive hearing loss: tone heard better in poorer ear

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Young children get middle ear infections more often than adults because their:
questions.rationale: Short, straight eustachian tubes let organisms reach the middle ear; serous otitis media is a common cause of hearing loss in children.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ear disorders (PDF p. 437)
questions.quote: Children are pmne to otitis media because of short eustachian tube.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An elderly man understands men's voices but not women's. This is typical of:
questions.rationale: Presbycusis is age-related sensorineural loss affecting high-pitched sounds first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Presbycusis (PDF p. 437)
questions.quote: Hearing loss is predominantly in high — pitched sounds. e.g., women's voice.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When talking with a client who has a hearing impairment, the nurse should:
options: Face him and speak in a normal tone
questions.rationale: Facing the client allows lip reading; a normal or lower tone is easier to hear than shouting or a high pitch.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Communicating with hearing impaired (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: Talk directly to the client, facing him/her. So that he/she could read lip movement.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A child has a mung bean stuck in his ear. Why is ear irrigation avoided?
questions.rationale: Vegetable matter absorbs water and expands, making removal harder; insects may be flushed out.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ear foreign bodies (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: If the foreign body is a vegetable seed, do not irrigate the ear. Vegetable seeds expand when exposed to warm water.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ear irrigation fluid should be at body temperature to prevent:
questions.rationale: Cold or hot fluid stimulates the vestibular system and causes vertigo; aim the flow at the canal wall.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ear irrigation (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: The solution used for ear irrigation should be at body temperature to prevent dizziness.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has attacks of vertigo with tinnitus, hearing loss and vomiting. Which diet is advised?
questions.rationale: Meniere's disease involves excess endolymph; low sodium and avoiding caffeine, alcohol and tobacco help.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Meniere's disease (PDF p. 439)
questions.quote: Low sodium diet is recommended. To prevent water retention.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After stapedectomy for otosclerosis, the nurse teaches the client to:
options: Shampoo the hair the next day
questions.rationale: Keep pressure off the middle ear: sneeze or cough with mouth open, avoid air travel and shampooing for about a week.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ear surgery (PDF p. 439)
questions.quote: Blow nose, sneeze, or cough with open mouth.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After ear surgery, the nurse asks the client to smile, wrinkle his forehead and close his eyes to check for:
questions.rationale: The facial nerve runs through the middle ear; asymmetry suggests injury.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 12 Ear surgery complications (PDF p. 439)
questions.quote: Ask to show teeth, wrinkle forehead, raise eyebrows, close the eyes.
